modeReason: The teen-chatbot-safety story reaches relevance 18 (novelty 2 x magnitude 3 x breadth 3), well above the fresh threshold of 8, so today stands on its own rather than continuing yesterday's doctor/bank-hack thread.
phrase: A technology company told employees to cut back on using a rival chatbot at work. The same week it gave its own chatbot more control over your files and computer.
phraseAlternatives: One company doesn't fully trust a rival's chatbot with its own secrets. It trusts its own chatbot with your files, your folders, and your operating system.
A company told workers to scale back a competitor's chatbot, then handed its own chatbot the keys to your files.
Workers were told to cut back on chatting with the rival AI. Meanwhile the house AI got permission to open your files and click your buttons.
Trust your own robot, the company says, while quietly trusting it with more of your computer than ever.

brief.concept: A company slows employees' access to a rival AI chatbot while quietly handing its own chatbot the keys to your files.
brief.metaphor: Trusting the house robot with everything, while only partly trusting someone else's.

brief.composition: Two-panel split scene. Left panel: a human office guard holds up a hand at a half-open office door to pause a small robot, which holds out an ID badge. Right panel: the same guard hands a second robot a large ring of keys, standing beside an open filing cabinet labeled FILES with papers spilling out. A soft vertical seam divides the two panels.
